summary: Former 30-ft fire tower on Dickinson Hill, Stanislaus/Merced area, CA; built and staffed in 1941 per newspaper excerpts; FFLA lists it as gone.

facts.design: Thirty-foot tower (1941 newspaper excerpt; cab not described)
facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as gone; no removal date or site description found
facts.agency: Forestry service (not named further in the 1941 excerpt)

events.note: Lookout station erected six miles east of Montpellier on the old Dickenson school property; a thirty-foot tower had been erected by the 25 June 1941 report
Robert Johnson of Oakland engaged to fill the lookout job under the forestry service; went on duty the Saturday before the 25 June 1941 report
Stanislaus County board order dated 10 June 1941: committed $200 toward maintaining the lookout, on condition that Merced County match it
Similar Stanislaus County board order dated 11 May 1942

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts files the site under Merced County, and its 1941 excerpt covers eastern Stanislaus County and adjacent Merced territory; the FFLA lists it under Stanislaus. The record keeps both counties.

notes_for_editor: Two WebSearch queries found only New York's Dickinson Hill Fire Tower (us-ny-dickinson-hill), a different tower; do not merge them. Source spells the town Montpeliter once and Montpellier elsewhere; the story uses Montpellier. The 30-ft height is converted to 9.1 m. The Forest Lookouts excerpts are transcriptions of newspapers and were not checked against the papers. The June 1941 and May 1942 board orders have near-identical wording and are presented as two dated orders. Not found: contractor, removal date, current condition, public access. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the story now says the supervisors set aside money for communications (not that they paid for them), the station was providing fire protection (not meant to protect), and the board committed $200 on condition of a Merced match (not offered); the lookout-station and supervisors sentences were reworded away from the excerpt's phrasing. Merced County placement is now quoted from the page heading. The June 1941 order's Stanislaus attribution is an inference from its wording, kept.
